newsitem.title: USA: Carnival makes offer for Celebrity Cruise.
newsitem.headline: Carnival makes offer for Celebrity Cruise.

text.p: Carnival Corp on Wednesday said it sent a proposal to the Chandris Group and Overseas Shipholding Group Inc offering to buy Celebrity Cruise Lines for $525 million.
The company said it would pay in cash or a combination of cash and stock, and that it would consider raising the price if it could identify additional value in Celebrity.
Last week, Royal Caribbean International announced an agreement to acquire Celebrity for $1.3 billion in cash and stock in a bid to become the leader in the vacation cruise business.

Carnival said in a statement Wednesday evening that it would work with Celebrity and its stockholders on an expedited basis to perform due diligence, finalize a proposal and enter a definitive agreement.
"There is a very strong strategic fit for Celebrity within the Carnival Corporation group of cruise lines," the company statement said.

The statement added that Carnival would maintain Celebrity as a separate brand under current management and said there should be "substantial opportunities" for Celebrity employees, including the management team.
Carnival said a successful acquisition of Celebrity should not have a dilutive effect on 1998 earnings.
Carnival shares closed down 3/16 Wednesday at 43-1/16. Those of Royal Caribbean closed down 5/8 at 36-7/8, and those of Overseas Shipholding closed unchanged at 19-5/6.
